key_insight: The paper establishes Lipschitz stability and uniqueness for two 3D wave-like coefficient inverse problems using data from a single point-source location, under a time-finite-difference assumption for an associated PDE.
engineering_relevance: These results support recovering spatially varying material coefficients with limited source access and provide globally convergent reconstruction methods.
method: Recover either a potential coefficient or a coefficient in the hyperbolic operator’s principal part.
Use data generated by one point source activated at time zero.
Develop numerical methods for both problems and prove global convergence.
evidence_signal: Extensive computational tests of the potential-recovery method report very accurate reconstructions of complicated media from noisy data, but the abstract gives no quantitative metrics.
watch_item: The theoretical results rely on an associated PDE discretized in time, and computational validation is reported only for potential recovery.
paper_title: Two 3-Dimensional Coefficient Inverse Problems for Wave-like Equations With a Single Location of the Point Source
